Start With a Diagnosis

Knee pain in Rajkot can affect walking, commuting, work, exercise, and household activities. Because pain may come from the joint, surrounding soft tissues, or referred pain from the hip or lower back, an evaluation should begin by identifying the likely cause before treatment is selected.

Common Causes of Knee Pain

Common causes include knee osteoarthritis, meniscus injury, ligament or tendon problems, inflammation, muscle weakness, repeated strain, and pain after an injury. Age-related cartilage changes may cause gradually increasing pain and stiffness, while an injury or inflammatory condition can cause more sudden symptoms.

When to Seek an Evaluation

Arrange a clinical evaluation if knee pain lasts more than a short period, keeps returning, or makes walking, stairs, work, or sleep difficult. Recurrent swelling, locking, clicking with pain, reduced movement, or a feeling that the knee may give way are also reasons to seek advice. Severe pain after an injury, an obvious deformity, inability to bear weight, or fever with a hot and swollen knee needs prompt medical attention.

How Knee Pain Is Evaluated

The clinician may ask when the symptoms began, which activities affect them, and what treatment has already been tried. Examination can assess the knee's movement, alignment, strength, tenderness, swelling, and stability, along with the hip and back when relevant. An X-ray or other imaging may be recommended when the history and examination indicate that it would help clarify the diagnosis.

Non-Surgical Management Options

Management is based on the underlying condition, symptom severity, daily function, and overall health. Options may include activity modification, guided exercise or physiotherapy, strengthening around the knee, weight management when relevant, and medicines advised by a clinician. Injections or other image-guided treatments may be discussed for selected patients after an assessment. The appropriate plan can change as symptoms and examination findings change.

Genicular Artery Embolization

Genicular Artery Embolization (GAE) is an image-guided, non-surgical procedure that may be considered for selected people with persistent knee osteoarthritis-related pain after appropriate evaluation and previous management. GAE is not suitable for every cause of knee pain, and a consultation is needed to discuss potential benefits, limitations, risks, and alternatives.
